title: Pet legacy-migration test fails on a database built from master_schema.sql alone
description:
`Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent` (`unittests/CuTest/test_database_persistence.c:792`) fails on a database that was built from `sql/master_schema.sql` alone, when the syntax-check boot has not run against that database first. It passes in the local CI matrix and in `make test-all`, where the boot runs before it.

Seen twice: in S5's verification (2026-09-30, "passes on rerun") and by the reviewer of MR !21 (2026-10-04). Reproduced on 2026-10-04 at `b485062c8`.

## Repro

```bash
docker run -d --rm --name petprobe -e MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=probe -e MARIADB_DATABASE=luminari_probe \
  -p 127.0.0.4:3306:3306 mariadb:10.11
docker exec -i petprobe mariadb -uroot -pprobe luminari_probe < sql/master_schema.sql
LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_ENABLE=1 LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_HOST=127.0.0.4 LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_PORT=3306 \
  LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_USER=root LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD=probe \
  LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_DATABASE=luminari_probe LUMINARI_TEST_SKIP_SYNTAX_BOOT=1 \
  CUTEST_FILTER=Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent ./cutest
```

```text
SYSERR: Required cascading foreign key pet_save_objs.pet_idnum -> pet_data.pet_data_id is missing
1) Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent: unittests/CuTest/test_database_persistence.c:872: assert failed
```

Line 872 is `CuAssertTrue(tc, first_verification)`: `verify_pet_persistence_schema()` fails right after `run_pet_persistence_migrations()` succeeded. A second run on the same database fails the same way.

## What is not known yet

Whether this is only the test's fixture (it relies on something a boot leaves in the database, such as rows of `schema_migrations` or the tables' boot-time shape), or the migrations themselves leave the foreign key out when they start from the `master_schema.sql` shape. The second would matter on a fresh install whose first boot goes through the same functions, so that is the first thing to check.

## Done when

The test passes alone on a database made from `master_schema.sql`, with and without the syntax-check boot before it, and the cause is named (fixture or migration).

title: An OLC save of an object prototype leaves its live objects sharing the prototype's lists
description:
## Problem

`add_object()` (`src/olc/genobj.c`) replaces an existing prototype and then calls
`update_all_objects()`, which writes the whole new prototype over every live object of that
prototype (`*obj = *refobj`) and puts back a list of runtime fields. The list is older than
several fields of `struct obj_data`. After the save, each live object of the prototype:

- shares the prototype's `special_abilities` list and `sbinfo` array. `read_object()` gives
  every object a copy of its own and `free_obj()` frees both with the object, so extracting one
  live object frees the prototype's list. The prototype, the other live objects and the next
  `read_object()` of that prototype then use freed memory, and a second extraction frees it
  again.
- has dropped its own `special_abilities`, `sbinfo`, `arcane_mark`, `restring_identifier`,
  restrung strings, script and `trap` without freeing them.
- has `next_in_hash` and `prev_in_hash` set to the prototype's NULL while it is still on its
  `obj_rnum_hash` chain. The chain is cut at that object, so `get_obj_num()` no longer finds
  the objects behind it, and `remove_obj_from_rnum_hash()` later empties the bucket or leaves a
  freed object on it.
- has lost `sheath_primary` and `sheath_secondary` (the sheathed weapons stay in `object_list`
  with nothing pointing to them), `next_gitem`, `limb_restore_slot` and the `rol_*` runtime
  state.

## Evidence

Run under valgrind on master `ee42019ed` on 2026-10-06, with a probe test: a prototype with
one special ability, one live object from `read_object()` that carries an arcane mark, then
`oedit_save_internally()`. After the save the live object's list pointer is the prototype's and
its mark is NULL. `extract_obj()` of the live object frees the block the prototype still points
to (an invalid read of the prototype's ability follows), and the object's own list and mark are
reported lost.

The spellbook array, the hash links, the sheath pointers and the other fields are read from the
code, not run.

## Proposed fix

Before the prototype is replaced, each live object releases what it owns, as `free_obj()` does.
After the copy it gets copies of its own of what `read_object()` copies, and every runtime-only
field is put back.

Found on 2026-10-06 while checking the callers of `free_object_strings()` for work item #15;
it is not part of that work.
